pathway.title: CLEVELAND-CLIFFS INC. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is the binding constraint, and it has improved through earnings, not repayment. Net debt of USD 7,568 million is 7.87x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 962 million and 7.79x the adjusted figure of USD 972 million, against 18.90x at the end of 2024, yet net debt is USD 372 million higher than at the end of 2025. Interest cover of 1.82x was 0.94x at June 2026, and only one quarter separates the two, so the cushion above 1.0x is recent. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C10; calculation C4; calculation C5; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Free cash flow conversion is the weakest dimension. Capital expenditure of USD 601 million and cash interest of USD 529 million total USD 1,130 million over the last twelve months against EBITDA of USD 962 million, a gap of USD 168 million before working capital, taxes and pensions, and free cash flow was USD 485 million negative; the ABL Facility funded the shortfall with net borrowings of USD 383 million in nine months. Planned capital spending is mostly sustaining, so there is limited room to cut it. Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 91

Earnings are driven by price and have recovered sharply, which supports the credit only if price holds. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 612 million in the third quarter, above the company's USD 575 million guide, with the domestic hot-rolled coil price at USD 1,195 per net ton against USD 851 for 2025, and only 35% to 40% of flat-rolled shipments are on fixed-price contracts. Shipments moved little across 2026, so the improvement is price and not demand. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_clf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; EX-99.1_2026-07-23_clf-202606308xkex991.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-19_clf-202609308xkex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13

Liquidity is adequate for the near term but rests on a borrowing base, and maturities are back-ended. Cash of USD 77 million and ABL borrowing capacity of USD 3,169 million give USD 3,246 million, but the borrowing base of USD 4,060 million sits USD 690 million below the commitment of USD 4,750 million and moves with receivables and inventory. The ABL Facility drawing of USD 834 million is the first maturity in June 2028, followed by USD 1,268 million of senior notes in 2029 and USD 750 million in 2030, which together are 36.98% of principal. Basis: calculation C9; calculation C14; calculation C13; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_clf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16

Ownership and financial policy neither add nor remove support. No sponsor is identified, governance risk is medium on mixed capital-allocation evidence, and USD 1.4 billion of the repurchase authorisation remains unused, so creditors rely on management's stated aim of cutting net debt to under 2.5x EBITDA by the middle of 2027, a target worded differently in the July and October releases. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-19_clf-202609308xkex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-07-23_clf-202606308xkex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

Own raw materials lower input-cost volatility but add fixed cost that an idling or a price fall exposes
Seven blast furnaces and four electric arc furnaces with configured capability of about 20.0 million net tons of raw steel a year
High fixed-cost base means margin is very sensitive to shipment volume and price
Four operating segments, one reportable (Steelmaking); Other Businesses cover tubular, tooling and stamping and European operations
Credit exposure is essentially the steelmaking segment
FY2025 revenue by market: direct automotive 30%, infrastructure and manufacturing 29%, distributors and converters 28%, steel producers 13%; FY2024: 32%, 27%, 28%, 13%
The company says automotive earns higher through-the-cycle margins; its share of revenue fell two percentage points in 2025
About 35% to 40% of flat-rolled steel shipments are under fixed-price contracts; the rest is spot or index-linked
Most volume reprices with the market, so earnings and coverage move quickly with price
Domestic hot-rolled coil averaged USD 1,195 per net ton in Q3 2026, 42% above Q3 2025 and the highest quarterly average since Q2 2022; USD 851 per net ton for 2025
Price recovery is the main source of the earnings improvement; a reversal would hit coverage first
Steel shipments of 3,770, 4,108, 4,025 and 4,150 thousand net tons in Q4 2025 and Q1 to Q3 2026; average selling price of USD 993, 1,048, 1,124 and 1,177 per net ton
Volume moved little across 2026 while price realised rose each quarter, so the recovery is price-led
Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,893 million (FY2023), 773 million (FY2024), 37 million (FY2025) and 993 million (nine months 2026)
Earnings are volatile, so leverage swings with the cycle
Iron ore pellets from own mines in Michigan and Minnesota, a direct reduction plant in Ohio, scrap facilities, a coal complex in West Virginia and coke plants
Internal feedstock gives cost stability against electric arc furnace producers that rely on imported metallics
More than 90% of about 20,000 hourly employees are union-represented; all open agreements were renegotiated in 2025; more site agreements expire in 2026
Renewals are a recurring risk to continuity of production

2025: six operations idled or closed; 2026: Gary plate finishing line, one Burns Harbor plate mill and Hamilton finishing operations idled; a slab contract of about 10% of volume expired on 2025-12-09
Lower fixed cost and a better mix, but idled-facility accruals of USD 40 million remain
Cash capital expenditure of USD 561 million in FY2025; 2026 plan of about USD 700 million
Capital spending is mostly sustaining, so little discretionary spend can be cut
50% Section 232 tariffs on steel imports; total steel imports through August 2026 down 15% year on year; Canadian tariff-rate quotas extended to June 2027
Trade protection supports domestic price, and its removal would be a downside trigger
Supplier finance obligations of USD 95 million at 2026-09-30 and USD 101 million at 2025-12-31
A withdrawal of the programs would unwind payables and draw on liquidity

runs.text: Strength: scale and integration. The company runs seven blast furnaces and four electric arc furnaces and sources most of its iron ore pellets from its own mines, which stabilises its main input cost against electric arc furnace producers that depend on imported metallics; this supports margin recovery when prices rise and lowers supply risk for automotive customers. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11

Strength: automotive franchise and price recovery. Direct automotive was 30% of 2025 revenue and the company says automotive steel typically earns higher through-the-cycle margins, and the 2026 price recovery lifted nine-month adjusted EBITDA to USD 993 million, which supports interest cover as long as price holds. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12

Strength: maturity profile and market access. No debt matures before June 2028, and in 2025 the company raised USD 1,975 million of notes and USD 951 million of equity, which shows access to both markets, at coupons above those of the notes due 2029 and 2030. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16

Weakness: leverage and coverage. Net leverage of 7.87x and cover of 1.82x leave little room for a price decline, and interest and capital spending exceed EBITDA over the last twelve months. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C7

Weakness: price exposure and cost. Only 35% to 40% of shipments are fixed-price, adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 37 million in 2025, and the latest quarterly report cites higher cost per ton, so margin gains rest on price. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41

Weakness: liquidity quality and unquantified repair levers. Liquidity depends on a borrowing base below the commitment, and the asset sales and POSCO transaction that management cites as debt-reduction routes have no stated amounts. Basis: calculation C14; Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-19_clf-202609308xkex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Two transactions shaped the balance sheet. The Stelco acquisition closed on November 1, 2024 for total purchase consideration of USD 3,208 million, made up of USD 2,450 million in cash, USD 343 million in shares and USD 415 million of debt consideration, and it roughly doubled the company's exposure to the North American spot market while adding Canadian operations whose results have been weak. The 2025 refinancing then issued USD 850 million of senior notes due 2031 in February 2025 and USD 1,125 million of senior notes due 2034 in September and October 2025, redeemed all USD 685 million of the remaining 2027 notes on October 3, 2025, and used net proceeds of USD 951 million from an equity issue on October 30, 2025 to repay borrowings under the ABL Facility. Basis: calculation C6; calculation C9; calculation C10; 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 124; 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 133–134; 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 140

No new notes were issued in the first nine months of 2026, and the nine-month cash flow shows net borrowings under the ABL Facility instead. Two possible transactions are open but unquantified: a strategic partnership with POSCO under a memorandum of understanding that still needs definitive agreements, and sales of non-core operating assets, idled facilities and inactive sites for which the company engaged an advisor in 2025. The October release also refers to property sale proceeds without stating an amount. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_clf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; EX-99.1_2026-10-19_clf-202609308xkex991.htm.jsonl, page 1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance fact pack for CLEVELAND-CLIFFS INC. (clf), as of 2026-11-05, for the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's business, ownership, operating model, transactions, events and governance evidence in the seven supplied annual, quarterly and release documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cleveland-Cliffs is an exchange-listed, vertically integrated North American steelmaker with no sponsor identified in the documents, so creditor protection rests on its own financial policy and operating recovery rather than on owner support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue follows the hot-rolled coil price: about 30% of 2025 revenue came from direct automotive customers and 28% from distributors and converters, and 35% to 40% of flat-rolled shipments are sold on fixed-price contracts, so earnings fell in 2025, when adjusted EBITDA was USD 37 million, and recovered with the 2026 price rise. Debt-funded growth in 2024, then equity and new notes in 2025, extended maturities and cut revolver drawings but leave the company relying on management's plan to repay debt from free cash flow and asset sales that no document quantifies.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a cyclical, price-taking steelmaker whose earnings, not owner support, carry the credit. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 1,893 million in 2023, USD 773 million in 2024 and USD 37 million in 2025 and reached USD 993 million in the first nine months of 2026, while the average hot-rolled coil price of USD 1,195 per net ton in the third quarter of 2026 was 42% above the year before and the highest quarterly average since 2022. Only 35% to 40% of flat-rolled shipments are on fixed-price contracts, so earnings follow price quickly in both directions, and creditors' coverage depends on the price holding. Direct automotive, which the company says earns higher through-the-cycle margins, was 28% of steelmaking revenue in the third quarter of 2026 against 34% for distributors and converters, whose revenue rose 42% on the year, so the revenue mix is shifting toward the distributor market and away from automotive.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management's claim of falling unit costs is only partly borne out by the quarterly cost discussion, so margin gains rest on price rather than cost. The report says cost per ton has fallen year over year since 2023, yet the same report attributes a USD 380 million rise in third-quarter cost of goods sold partly to higher cost per ton from mix and repair and maintenance, and a USD 300 million rise over nine months to energy, repair and maintenance and mix. If price falls, creditors cannot assume a lower cost base will cushion it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor or controlling shareholder is identified, so there is no sponsor-willingness question, but share ownership and board control are not established. The documents show a listed company with a combined chairman, president and chief executive role and an auditor's clean opinion on internal control, while directors, pay and share ownership sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied. Without a sponsor there is no sponsor-fee or dividend-recapitalisation channel to read, and also no equity backstop beyond what the public market provides, as the 2025 equity issue showed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation has been mixed: the company repurchased USD 733 million of shares in 2024 and paid USD 2,450 million in cash for Stelco with debt, then repaired the balance sheet in 2025 with an equity issue of USD 951 million, USD 1,975 million of new notes and the redemption of USD 685 million of 2027 notes. The repair shows willingness to use equity to lower leverage, but USD 1.4 billion of the repurchase authorisation remains available, and no repurchases were made in the first nine months of 2026. The ABL Facility contains covenants on dividends and share repurchases, but the debt documents were not supplied, so how much room remains to resume repurchases is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management's route to lower debt is stated but unquantified: free cash flow, a possible transaction with POSCO and sales of non-core assets. The October release expects a major debt reduction in the fourth quarter using free cash flow and property sale proceeds, but no amount, buyer or date is stated, and the POSCO memorandum remains subject to definitive agreements. Until a transaction is signed the proceeds are upside, not a source of repayment creditors can count.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Footprint changes and labour terms add execution risk but look manageable. The company idled or closed six operations in 2025 and, in 2026, idled a plate finishing line, one plate mill and the Hamilton finishing operations, while an unprofitable slab contract that was about 10% of sales volume expired in December 2025. More than 90% of the hourly workforce is represented by unions, all open agreements were renegotiated in 2025 without disruption, and further site agreements expire in 2026, so a stoppage would hit a business whose adjusted EBITDA was only USD 37 million in 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Non-debt claims are modest relative to debt but need monitoring. Supplier finance programs stood at USD 95 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 101 million at the end of 2025, and the Stelco acquisition brought employee benefit funding commitments with a carrying liability of USD 158 million and fixed payments running to 2042. Stelco also holds an option to buy a quarter of the MinnTac iron ore mine for USD 500 million until January 31, 2027, which would be a call on liquidity if exercised, though the option's fair value has fallen to USD 16 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is the speed of the recovery and management's guidance. Third-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 612 million was USD 37 million above the USD 575 million guided in July, the company expects about USD 715 million in the fourth quarter and more than USD 4 billion in 2027, and the hot-rolled coil price is far above its 2025 average of USD 851 per net ton. If those expectations hold, leverage would fall quickly without any asset sale, and no sponsor is identified that could extract cash from the company. The view would improve on a signed POSCO transaction with proceeds applied to debt and worsen if the hot-rolled coil price fell back toward its 2025 level, if Stelco's contribution turned negative again after the galvanizing idling, or if the repurchase authorisation were used before debt is reduced.

fields.value: - No indentures, credit agreement or guarantor schedule were supplied, so restrictions on distributions, repurchases and asset transfers are not established, which means legal capacity for value transfer is unassessed and the view on creditor alignment rests on behaviour alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer concentration is not disclosed in the documents read, so the automotive exposure is stated by revenue share only and the durability of the largest customer relationships cannot be judged.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management's expectations for the fourth quarter, 2027 and debt reduction are management language and are not tested here, so the recovery view depends on guidance the documents give no way to verify.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Cleveland-Cliffs presents medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is the combination of debt-funded growth and share repurchases in 2024 followed by an equity-funded repair in 2025, which matters because it raised leverage before earnings fell and shows the company will use equity to cure it, and it implies refinancing risk that depends on earnings recovery rather than on any owner commitment. Countervailing evidence is the clean opinion on internal control, steady quarterly reporting with reconciliations of non-GAAP measures, and no repurchases in 2025 or the first nine months of 2026. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the indentures and the credit agreement. Governance assessment completed with limitations; sponsor and governance risk level: medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two transactions shaped the balance sheet. The Stelco acquisition closed on November 1, 2024 for total purchase consideration of USD 3,208 million, made up of USD 2,450 million in cash, USD 343 million in shares and USD 415 million of debt consideration, and it roughly doubled the company's exposure to the North American spot market while adding Canadian operations whose results have been weak. The 2025 refinancing then issued USD 850 million of senior notes due 2031 in February 2025 and USD 1,125 million of senior notes due 2034 in September and October 2025, redeemed all USD 685 million of the remaining 2027 notes on October 3, 2025, and used net proceeds of USD 951 million from an equity issue on October 30, 2025 to repay borrowings under the ABL Facility.

Two possible transactions are open but unquantified: a strategic partnership with POSCO under a memorandum of understanding that still needs definitive agreements, and sales of non-core operating assets, idled facilities and inactive sites for which the company engaged an advisor in 2025. The October release also refers to property sale proceeds without stating an amount.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for CLEVELAND-CLIFFS INC. (clf), as of 2026-11-05, for the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business profile, financial profile, downside path and monitoring triggers drawn from the supplied annual, quarterly and release documents and the three earlier module outputs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cleveland-Cliffs is a scaled, integrated steelmaker whose credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 7.87x and negative free cash flow, so creditors depend on steel prices staying high through 2027 to rebuild coverage before the ABL Facility matures in June 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C8; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is adequate: scale, own iron ore and an automotive franchise support cash generation, and the price rise of 2026 lifted nine-month adjusted EBITDA to USD 993 million from USD 37 million for all of 2025. The financial profile is weak at present: interest cover is 1.82x, capital spending and cash interest together exceed EBITDA, and liquidity of USD 3,246 million depends on a borrowing base. Maturities are back-ended, so the near-term question is cash flow, not refinancing dates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C9; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_clf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is the binding constraint, and it has improved through earnings, not repayment. Net debt of USD 7,568 million is 7.87x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 962 million and 7.79x the adjusted figure of USD 972 million, against 18.90x at the end of 2024, yet net debt is USD 372 million higher than at the end of 2025. Interest cover of 1.82x was 0.94x at June 2026, and only one quarter separates the two, so the cushion above 1.0x is recent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C10; calculation C4; calculation C5; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow conversion is the weakest dimension. Capital expenditure of USD 601 million and cash interest of USD 529 million total USD 1,130 million over the last twelve months against EBITDA of USD 962 million, a gap of USD 168 million before working capital, taxes and pensions, and free cash flow was USD 485 million negative; the ABL Facility funded the shortfall with net borrowings of USD 383 million in nine months. Planned capital spending is mostly sustaining, so there is limited room to cut it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 91

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are driven by price and have recovered sharply, which supports the credit only if price holds. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 612 million in the third quarter, above the company's USD 575 million guide, with the domestic hot-rolled coil price at USD 1,195 per net ton against USD 851 for 2025, and only 35% to 40% of flat-rolled shipments are on fixed-price contracts. Shipments moved little across 2026, so the improvement is price and not demand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_clf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; EX-99.1_2026-07-23_clf-202606308xkex991.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-19_clf-202609308xkex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for the near term but rests on a borrowing base, and maturities are back-ended. Cash of USD 77 million and ABL borrowing capacity of USD 3,169 million give USD 3,246 million, but the borrowing base of USD 4,060 million sits USD 690 million below the commitment of USD 4,750 million and moves with receivables and inventory. The ABL Facility drawing of USD 834 million is the first maturity in June 2028, followed by USD 1,268 million of senior notes in 2029 and USD 750 million in 2030, which together are 36.98% of principal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C9; calculation C14; calculation C13; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_clf-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership and financial policy neither add nor remove support. No sponsor is identified, governance risk is medium on mixed capital-allocation evidence, and USD 1.4 billion of the repurchase authorisation remains unused, so creditors rely on management's stated aim of cutting net debt to under 2.5x EBITDA by the middle of 2027, a target worded differently in the July and October releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-19_clf-202609308xkex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-07-23_clf-202606308xkex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the pace of recovery and the company's expectations. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 612 million in the third quarter beat the guide, and the company expects about USD 715 million in the fourth quarter, more than USD 4 billion in 2027, a major debt reduction in the fourth quarter from free cash flow and property sale proceeds, and substantial proceeds if the POSCO transaction proceeds. The 2025 comparison is also less severe than it looks: at the 2025 average hot-rolled coil price of USD 851 per net ton the company earned only USD 37 million of adjusted EBITDA, but that year carried an unprofitable slab contract that has since ended and the company has since idled mines and finishing lines, so the same price could now earn more. The view would improve if the fourth quarter delivers positive free cash flow and net debt starts to fall, and it would worsen if the hot-rolled coil price returned toward its 2025 level, if free cash flow stayed negative after the fourth quarter, or if the repurchase authorisation were used before debt falls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: scale and integration. The company runs seven blast furnaces and four electric arc furnaces and sources most of its iron ore pellets from its own mines, which stabilises its main input cost against electric arc furnace producers that depend on imported metallics; this supports margin recovery when prices rise and lowers supply risk for automotive customers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: automotive franchise and price recovery. Direct automotive was 30% of 2025 revenue and the company says automotive steel typically earns higher through-the-cycle margins, and the 2026 price recovery lifted nine-month adjusted EBITDA to USD 993 million, which supports interest cover as long as price holds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: maturity profile and market access. No debt matures before June 2028, and in 2025 the company raised USD 1,975 million of notes and USD 951 million of equity, which shows access to both markets, at coupons above those of the notes due 2029 and 2030.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: leverage and coverage. Net leverage of 7.87x and cover of 1.82x leave little room for a price decline, and interest and capital spending exceed EBITDA over the last twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: price exposure and cost. Only 35% to 40% of shipments are fixed-price, adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 37 million in 2025, and the latest quarterly report cites higher cost per ton, so margin gains rest on price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: liquidity quality and unquantified repair levers. Liquidity depends on a borrowing base below the commitment, and the asset sales and POSCO transaction that management cites as debt-reduction routes have no stated amounts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cleveland-Cliffs is a vertically integrated flat-rolled steel producer focused on automotive sheet steel, with seven blast furnaces and four electric arc furnaces in the United States and Canada and mostly self-supplied iron ore. Integration stabilises the main raw material cost, which supports margin when prices rise, but the Stelco acquisition of 2024 added Canadian capacity with more spot sales and a market that weakened in 2025, which adds earnings volatility. It has no identified sponsor or controlling shareholder, the chairman, president and chief executive roles are held by one person, and directors and share ownership sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so financial policy is read from behaviour: debt-funded growth and share repurchases in 2024, then equity and notes in 2025, and no repurchases since.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 124; 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 157; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical and price-led. Direct automotive was 30% of 2025 revenue, infrastructure and manufacturing 29%, distributors and converters 28% and steel producers 13%, and 35% to 40% of flat-rolled shipments are on fixed-price contracts that are typically annual or multi-year, with the rest on spot or index prices. Most volume therefore reprices with the hot-rolled coil index, so revenue moves with price while shipments stay near the same level, and revenue is not a stable base for fixed charges, though the automotive contracts add some visibility. The annual report flags concentration of customers in the automotive industry as a risk, but concentration by individual customer is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Much of the cost base does not move with price: from the first to the third quarter of 2026 steelmaking revenue rose by USD 690 million while cash cost of goods sold rose by USD 141 million, and depreciation, depletion and amortization is guided at about USD 1.1 billion for 2026 and selling and administrative expense at about USD 575 million. The same asymmetry works in reverse when price falls, so margin swings are larger than revenue swings: adjusted EBITDA fell from USD 773 million in 2024 to USD 37 million in 2025 on a revenue decline of 3.00%, and the last-twelve-months adjusted margin is 4.84%. Management says cost per ton has fallen each year since 2023, but the latest quarterly report cites higher cost per ton in the third quarter from mix and repair expense, so margin resilience is not demonstrated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C17; calculation C16; calculation C15; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-04-20_clf-202603318xkex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-04-20_clf-202603318xkex991.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-19_clf-202609308xkex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_clf-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA has not converted into free cash flow: free cash flow was USD 1,023 million negative in 2025 and USD 485 million negative over the last twelve months, because capital expenditure, cash interest and working capital absorb more than EBITDA when prices are low and receivables rebuild as prices recover. Capital expenditure is guided at about USD 700 million for 2026, mostly sustaining, cash interest is USD 529 million, and cash pension and other postretirement payments are guided at about USD 125 million, so only EBITDA that stays above this combined burden with stable working capital produces cash for debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C11; calculation C8; calculation C6; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-04-20_clf-202603318xkex991.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 91

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is set by trade policy. The domestic hot-rolled coil price rose 42% from a year earlier to USD 1,195 per net ton on subdued imports, 50% Section 232 tariffs and a 15% fall in imports through August 2026, so pricing power comes from protection and not from a cost advantage, and removal of the tariffs would reverse the earnings recovery that supports cover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New entrants are a limited threat. Integrated blast furnace capacity is costly to build, and the electric arc furnace capacity that is growing in the United States depends on busheling scrap that averaged USD 465 per long ton in the third quarter against a ten-year average of about USD 400, whereas the company sources most of its iron feedstock from its own mines, which holds its cost steadier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Substitutes matter little today. Aluminium and other materials compete in some manufactured products, but the company reports a shift away from aluminium in automotive and a trial in which its steel was stamped into exposed parts on a customer's aluminium-forming equipment and then moved to routine production, so substitution is not a primary credit driver on the evidence read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power sits with large automotive and distributor customers, who are 58% of 2025 revenue and buy under annual or multi-year contracts for 35% to 40% of shipments; management expects those contracts to reset higher for 2027, but customer concentration is not established, so the strength of that reset is unproven.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_clf-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; EX-99.1_2026-07-23_clf-202606308xkex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-19_clf-202609308xkex991.htm.jsonl, page 3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is limited for iron ore and higher for labour and energy. The company produces most of its own iron ore pellets, but more than 90% of its hourly workforce is unionised and negotiations with the United Steelworkers to renew expiring agreements are under way, so a stoppage or a costly settlement would pressure margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and regulatory factors are the material outside influence: United States tariffs, Canadian tariff-rate quotas extended to June 2027 and a rescoped Department of Energy grant for Middletown Works each change price or capital needs. Economic factors act through the hot-rolled coil price and automotive demand, and the war with Iran is raising global steel costs and freight, which makes imports less attractive. Social factors act through labour agreements, and technological factors are not established as a primary credit driver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Credit-translated SWOT. Strengths are scale, own iron ore, the automotive franchise, no maturity before June 2028 and proven access to equity and notes. Weaknesses are leverage, negative free cash flow, price exposure on fixed cost and borrowing-base-dependent liquidity. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the POSCO transaction, property and other asset sales and the end of a slab contract that was unprofitable in 2025. Threats are a reversal of trade protection or of the hot-rolled coil price, a stoppage or costly settlement in the 2026 labour renewals and use of the repurchase authorisation before debt falls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are scale, integration and the maturity profile, which give time for the price recovery to work. The constraints are leverage, coverage and cash conversion, which leave the company dependent on price. The trend is improving on price but not yet on debt, because net debt is higher than at the end of 2025. The key missing data are customer concentration, covenant terms, ratings and per-ton costs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C10; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For the next twelve to twenty-four months the company expects about USD 715 million of adjusted EBITDA in the fourth quarter and more than USD 4 billion in 2027 on 2027 contract changes and prevailing price forecasts; these are management expectations and would support cover and deleveraging if met. Tailwinds are tariff protection, low imports, the end of the slab contract and the Canadian tariff-rate quotas. Headwinds are the exposure to price, the 2026 labour renewals, the weak Canadian market for value-added sheet products that led to an indefinite idle of finishing operations at Hamilton Works, the USD 1 billion Middletown Works investment of which the company funds half under a Department of Energy framework that is not final, and the option for Stelco to buy a quarter of the MinnTac mine for USD 500 million, exercisable until January 2027. Over three to five years the company points to rare-earth exploration and its electrical steel business, neither of which is quantified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer-specific downside is a return of domestic hot-rolled coil toward its 2025 average of USD 851 per net ton while shipments hold near the 2026 level. Because only 35% to 40% of flat-rolled shipments are on fixed-price contracts, most revenue per ton would fall with the index while cost does not, so adjusted EBITDA would move toward the USD 37 million earned at that price in 2025 and free cash flow toward the USD 1,023 million outflow of that year. As an illustration of scale, one such year would use 31.52% of today's USD 3,246 million of liquidity, and the borrowing base would shrink as receivables and inventory fall, so usable liquidity would fall by more than the cash outflow alone. Management's levers are cutting the capital plan of about USD 700 million, which is mostly sustaining, selling assets and borrowing under the ABL Facility. Liquidity covers at least a year of such outflows by a wide margin, so distress is not indicated within the next year, but the cover shortens if the borrowing base shrinks, leverage would rise well above 7.87x and the June 2028 ABL maturity would arrive with weak coverage. The 2025 outcome also carried the slab contract that has since ended, so the loss could be smaller. The observable triggers are the hot-rolled coil price, quarterly free cash flow and borrowing-base availability.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Cleveland-Cliffs presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, own iron ore and an automotive franchise, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 7.87x, interest cover of 1.82x and negative free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears weak because most volume reprices with the market and costs are fixed. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding the 2026 price level through the June 2028 ABL maturity and on the debt reduction management expects, since the 2029 notes follow soon after. The primary downside path is a fall in hot-rolled coil toward its 2025 level while the borrowing base shrinks. Further analysis would require the debt agreements, ratings, customer concentration and a forward model. Top risk: price-driven earnings against a high fixed charge burden.
